title: AI changes reach users in stages, and each confirmed failure becomes an eval case
subtitle: Real code from Lomem's language app. Boxes marked example use made-up numbers.
aria: New AI behaviour first runs in shadow mode on real chats while the user still sees the old result, then a person reads the disagreements against a bar written first, then a flag flips only when an eval clears four fixed bars, then a canary widens from 5 to 100 percent while quality is no worse. After release, feedback tied to the exact turn is triaged by a person and every confirmed failure becomes an eval case that every later gate run checks. New checks start in log mode and enforce only under a 15 percent refusal rate.

build.title: A wrong answer looks right
build.text: A wrong model answer is a fast HTTP 200 with valid JSON. Error rates and latency stay flat, so they cannot catch it.

build.title: Shadow mode, then a readout
build.text: A judge model grades each real chat in shadow mode. The learner waits 0 s and still sees the rules' level. A person reads the disagreements against a bar written first.

build.title: A flag behind an eval gate, then a canary
build.text: `TD_JUDGE_MARKS` stays false until the gate clears four bars fixed in advance. A canary then widens from 5% to 100% of customers while the discard rate is no worse (example).

build.title: Each confirmed failure becomes an eval case
build.text: Real users send feedback tied to its session and turn. A person triages it, and a confirmed failure becomes a fixture row that every gate run checks. A weekly rerun is proposed, because the provider can change the model.

build.title: New checks start in log mode
build.text: A new guard first logs the refusal it would make. It is enforced only when its refusal rate is under 15% in every language and level.

route.title: Start the judge once, then answer without waiting
route.text: When the chat reaches its wind-down, the server claims the judge by writing a start time. The claim succeeds only once per chat. The tutor's reply goes back without waiting for the judge.

route.title: The judge reads the answers, never the rules' level
route.text: The judge gets the answered turns and their facts, but not the rules' level, so it cannot copy it. In the real test it replies B2 and cites turns 5 and 7.

route.title: Code checks whether the judge's level has evidence
route.text: Two or more levels from the rules is rejected. One level up needs two cited turns that pass the B2 check and no failed B2 question. Rules B1, judge B2: accepted.

route.title: Store the comparison next to the answer
route.text: The server writes `judge_level` B2 and `judge_would_change` true, only in the judge's own columns. Later someone can count disagreements without re-running anything.

route.title: The learner still sees the rules' level
route.text: Nothing the judge says reaches the learner yet: the learner sees B1. If the judge fails, the server logs it and keeps the rules' level.

route.title: A person reads the disagreements against a bar written first
route.text: The team counts `judge_would_change`: 38 of 412 chats (example). A person reads each one against the bar, right in ≥ 30 of 38. Lomem dropped its real judge the same day, and no learner saw a change.
